findings.detail: The notice is appended to `analystMessages` as `{ role: 'assistant', content }`. On the next turn, `handleAnalystSend` builds `historyContext` from `newHistory.slice(-6)` (line 402) and labels every assistant entry `Analyst:` — so the model is told its own previous answer was `Model "gemini-3.1-flash" is unavailable; continuing on "...". Output quality may differ.` That both consumes one of only six history slots and invites the model to respond to a maintenance message as if it were part of the analysis. The second consequence is visual: the notice renders through the same white assistant bubble at line 658, so a user cannot tell a system notice from an answer. Trigger is narrow (only after a real model retirement), which is why this is medium rather than high; it would be high if the window were larger or the notice were re-emitted per turn.
findings.summary: Fallback notice is stored as an assistant turn, so it re-enters the prompt

findings.detail: Two things weaken the announcement this change is trying to add. First, the `role="status"` element only enters the DOM when `geminiStatus === 'no-model'`, so the region and its text appear in the same commit; the ARIA practice is that a live region must already be in the accessibility tree for an insertion to be reliably announced, and several screen-reader/browser pairs stay silent on a region mounted with content. Second, the comment's own premise — 'a screen reader user presses Test and hears nothing at all' — still holds for the other three outcomes: `valid`, `invalid` and `quota` (lines 86-93) are badge-only with no live region, so the most common results of pressing Test remain unannounced while the rarest one is announced.
findings.summary: Live region is created at the same moment as its content, and covers 1 of 4 statuses

findings.detail: `advancePastRetiredModel` (services/geminiService.ts:312) builds the notice as a hardcoded English sentence, which was fine while its destinations were `console.warn` and a log panel. This diff promotes it to user-facing chat content in a component that takes `language` and sets `dir="rtl"` for Arabic (line 509), and every other string in that transcript comes from `t`. An Arabic user gets one English LTR sentence mid-conversation, inside an RTL container.
findings.summary: English-only notice posted into a transcript that supports Arabic

findings.detail: The new poll body — `box ? Math.round(box.x + box.width) : null` with `timeout: 10_000` — is character-for-character the helper `drawerRightEdge` at line 22, which three tests in the same file already use (lines 186, 198). The only reason not to call it is the custom failure message. Keeping a second copy is how the two drift: a future change to what 'off-canvas' means has to be made in two places, and the file currently teaches both patterns.
findings.summary: Inline poll duplicates the drawerRightEdge helper defined in the same file

findings.detail: The comment is right that the old title overclaimed — but the fix removes the claim rather than the gap. `SupportChat` has no test anywhere (no file under `tests/` or `e2e/` references it), so the exact failure the comment describes — the service contract green while the component passes no callback — is still undetectable, only now for the opposite reason: nothing asserts the component forwards it or renders the result. The service-level tests in this block are the ones that catch a dropped callback; none of them can catch a dropped call site.
findings.summary: The wiring this PR adds has no test; the rename records the gap without closing it

findings.detail: Two small regressions in an otherwise correct repair of these rows. The description previously linked `[ADR-0006](../adr/ADR-0006-model-tiers-not-model-ids.md)` and now says plain `ADR-0006`, so the register no longer navigates to the decision it rests on (TD-037 in the same table still links its ADR, so this is now inconsistent within the file). And 'every caller logs it as a warning' is not true of the caller this PR adds — SupportChat has no log panel and posts the notice into the transcript, which is the whole point of the code comment at line 448.
findings.summary: TD-041 row loses the ADR-0006 link and overstates the caller behaviour
